episode_summary: The hosts interview Roger Ver of Bitcoin.com about why he considers Bitcoin Cash better money than Bitcoin Core, the block size debate, Lightning Network capacity and merchant adoption, SegWit and the SegWit2x deal, Moore's law and on-chain scaling, and the Bitcoin.com labelling controversy. The episode also covers a Reddit story about cashing out bitcoin for a Mercedes.

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver predicted that multiple blockchains would share the market, with one, two or three of them holding the lion's share.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: I think there'll be lots of blockchains for lots of different things. But I think one, two, or three of those blockchains will have the lion's share of the market.

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver predicted that Bitcoin Cash would surpass Bitcoin Core in total value stored within about one and a half years.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: Bitcoin Cash is going to surpass Bitcoin Core in terms of the total amount of value being stored with it

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said he was so bullish that Bitcoin Cash would be the cryptocurrency most people use as cash around the world.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: I'm so bullish that Bitcoin Cash is the one that's most likely to get the most adoption and the most people around the world using it as cash

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver predicted that more of the world would use Bitcoin Cash as money than Bitcoin Core.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: is going to start using Bitcoin Cash as money than Bitcoin Core, simply because

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said Bitcoin Cash was plainly better money than Bitcoin Core, whatever the coins were called.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: bitcoin cash is just plain better money no matter what you call it

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said only around 17 bitcoin were tied up in the Lightning Network.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: there's only around 17 Bitcoin tied up in the Lightning Network

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said there were maybe three web shops accepting Lightning, compared with over 100,000 sites accepting Bitcoin Cash.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: maybe three web shops that accept it, compared to 100,000-plus sites that accept Bitcoin Cash for payments

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said the Bitcoin Core team intentionally undermined on-chain transactions, pushing users toward altcoins instead of Lightning.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: the Bitcoin Core team intentionally undermined the usefulness of those on-chain transactions

cards.claim: In May 2018 a host said the one-megabyte Bitcoin block size was probably too small, and that not raising it had been a poor decision.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: The core block size of one megabyte is probably too small.

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said on-chain capacity would take at least 10 years to fill, so on-chain scaling would remain a long-term solution.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: It's probably going to be at least 10 years before we come anywhere even remotely close to filling up what's possible right now today with the transactions on-chain

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver argued that blockchains are inherently serial, so base-layer scaling could not keep up with the parallel computing trend.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: doing a blockchain is inherently serial. You have to do things sequentially

cards.claim: In May 2018 a host said increasing the block size was not the final answer, and Roger Ver said he would disagree.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: increasing the block size is not the final answer period

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said layer one had been strangled and layer two solutions were not yet available.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: layer one has been strangled and the layer two solutions aren't available yet

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said the network could handle 100 megabyte blocks without any problem.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: could handle 100 megabyte blocks without any problem whatsoever

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said the market, not a couple of Bitcoin developers, should decide the block size.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: I think the market should decide, not a couple of Bitcoin wizards

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said Bitcoin Cash had an acceptance advantage over privacy coins because Bitcoin is in its name.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: that it already has acceptance because it has Bitcoin right there in the name

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said he sold his Lamborghini to buy more bitcoin, having owned it before bitcoin was invented.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: I had a Lamborghini before Bitcoin had even been invented. And I sold my Lamborghini to buy more Bitcoin

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said he had given 1,000 bitcoin to the Foundation for Economic Education, worth about $1.2 to $1.3 million at the time.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: I gave 1,000 big coins to the Foundation for Economic Education

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said Bitcoin Core supporters did not understand the underlying economics, so he moved his store of value into Bitcoin Cash.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: I watched the Bitcoin core people, not because they're bad people. It's just because they don't understand the underlying economics

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver recounted that Lightning Labs CEO Elizabeth Stark called paying for coffee on Lightning stupid.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: And she said, that's stupid. Why would you want to even do that?

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said Bitcoin.com then had almost 100 people on its payroll.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: So at Bitcoin.com now we have almost 100 people on the payroll

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said nobody was misled by Bitcoin.com's labelling and that a threatened lawsuit over it was ridiculous.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: Nobody's being misled. There's no victim there.

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said he supported Bitcoin Cash because it works as money, not because it matches Satoshi's white paper.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: So I don't support Bitcoin Cash because it's in line with the white paper.

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said SegWit had never gotten more than about 35% of miners signaling for it before the SegWit2x agreement.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: And up to that point, SegWit had never really gotten more than maybe 35% of the miners around the world signaling for it

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said Bitcoin Cash would not have gotten any traction without the SegWit2x bait and switch.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: Bitcoin Cash wouldn't have been anything. It wouldn't have gotten any traction at all had there not been a bait and switch in regards to the SegWit2x thing

cards.claim: In May 2018 an unidentified speaker said Satoshi was not God, though the white paper still defines what the words mean.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: Satoshi is not God, although I do think we can still look at the white paper for the definitions of what the words mean

cards.claim: In May 2018 Roger Ver said Bitcoin Cash does not need SegWit to fix transaction malleability, and could add Lightning later.
cards.speaker: Roger Ver
cards.quote: Bitcoin Cash doesn't necessarily need segregated witness to fix transaction malleability

title: TBP #202 - Roger Ver
